==English==
[[file:Man with iranian Thirty years ago fashion.jpg|250px|thumbnail|right|Man with '''moustache''' and [[sideburns]]]]
[[File:DieFilmwoche1928 6.png|thumb|The '''moustache''' of {{w|Charlie Chaplin}}]]

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|mustache||US}}

===Etymology===
Used in English since the 16th century. From {{bor|en|frm|moustache}} from {{der|en|it|mostaccio}}, from {{der|en|la-eme|mustācium}}, from {{der|en|gkm|μουστάκιον}}, diminutive of (Doric) {{der|en|grc|μύσταξ|t=upper lip}}, of unknown origin (probably a {{der|en|qsb-grc}} substrate). Replaced native {{ncog|en|kemp|t=moustache}}, from {{ncog|ang|cenep}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/məˈstɑːʃ/|/məˈstɒʃ/|a=SSB}}
* {{IPA|en|/məˈstæʃ/|a=Northern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈmʌstæʃ/|/məˈstæʃ/|a=US}}
** {{audio|en|En-us-moustache.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/məˈstɐːʃ/|a=AU}}
* {{IPA|en|/məˈstaːʃ/|a=NZ}}
* {{IPA|en|/məˈstaʃ/|/mʊstaʃ/|/mʌstaʃ/|a=CA}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɑːʃ|ɒʃ|æʃ|s1=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q15179}}A growth of [[facial hair]] between the nose and the upper lip.
#* {{RQ:Doyle Adventures of Gerard|chapter=How the Brigadier Triumphed in England|passage=A moment later there entered a tall thin Englishman with a great '''moustache''', which was a rare thing amid that clean-shaven race.}}
#* {{RQ:Chambers Younger Set|IX|passage=“A tight little craft,” was Austin’s invariable comment on the matron;{{nb...}}. ¶ Near her wandered her husband, orientally bland, invariably affable, and from time to time squinting sideways, as usual, in the ever-renewed expectation that he might catch a glimpse of his stiff, retroussé '''moustache'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Forster Howards End|passage=A hint of the truth broke on him after Sedan, when he saw the dyed '''moustaches''' of Napoleon going grey; another when he entered Paris, and saw the smashed windows of the Tuileries.}}
#* {{RQ:Chesterton Innocence of Father Brown|chapter=The Secret Garden|passage=Ivan, the confidential man with the scar and the '''moustaches''', came out of the house like a cannon ball, and came racing across the lawn to Valentin like a dog to his master.}}
#* {{RQ:Wharton Custom of the Country|passage=Small, well-knit, fair, he sat stroking his slight blond '''moustache''' and looking at her with kindly, almost tender eyes; but he left it to his sister and the others to draw her out and fit her into the pattern.}}
# {{lb|en|computing|informal}} A [[curly bracket]], {{m|mul|{}} or {{m|mul|}}}.

====Usage notes====
* The plural forms {{m|en|moustaches}} and {{m|en|mustaches}}, while formerly popular equivalents for the facial hair on a man's upper lip, are now archaic, with the singular preferred.

====Derived terms====
